title: L0-09 · Hamza, madda, alif maqṣūra, tanwīn, alif waṣla

blocks.text: L0-09 · Hamza, madda, alif maqṣūra, tanwīn, alif waṣla
Lesson overview

This unit completes the spelling: the glottis stroke (hamza) and its supports, the madda, the ā final written with ⁧ى⁩ , indeterminate terminations (tanwīn), the alife that is pronounced only at the beginning of the sentence and the small alif above some frequent words. After this drive you can read any text spoken.

rows: 7 hours · one week at a standard rate (recommended 1–2 days more)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, calligraphy L0-09, Anki deck (tag L0-09)
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. pronounce the hamza as a glottis stroke and distinguish it from ⁧ع⁩ ;
2. read the hamza on all media ( ⁧أ إ ؤ ئ ء⁩ ) and recognise the most common cases;
3. read ⁧آ⁩ , ⁧ى⁩ and alif short above the consonant ( ⁧هٰذَا⁩ );
4. read the tanwīn and know when it falls on pause;
5. apply the alif waṣla in the linked reading (wa-l-, fi-, bi-smi).

rows: Section 1: the hamza and the supports

blocks.text: 7 Correction · Anki
1. The hamza ⁧ء⁩

The sound. /ʔ/, the glottis stroke: the vocal cords close completely for a moment and then open again. It's the interruption you hear in English between the two parts of "uh-oh" . In the transliteration is written ʾ (closed apex), other than ʿ of the ⁧ع⁩ . She's a consonant. ⁧رَئِيس⁩ raʾīs has two syllables, ra-ʾīs, separated by a glottis stroke; Reading it with a single syllable is an error of pronunciation and, often, of speech. The words that begin with vowels. In Arabic no syllable begins with vowel: the words that seem to you to start with a, i, u begin with a hamza: ⁧أَمْن⁩ ʾamn Safety. By convention the initial hamza is not written in the transliteration: amn.
1.1 About what the hamza is written

The hamza can be alone on the line ( ⁧ء⁩ ) or on a support: ⁧ا⁩ ( ⁧أ⁩ , ⁧إ⁩ ), ⁧و⁩ ( ⁧ؤ⁩ ), ⁧ي⁩ no points ( ⁧ئ⁩ ). To read, just know that the support is not pronounced: only the glottis stroke counts with his vowel. The following rules are needed to write, valid in the vast majority of cases.

rows: Always on alif: ⁧أ⁩ with a or u, ⁧إ⁩ with i (the hamza below)
End of word, after long vowel or sukūn
End of word, after short vowel
Previous voice support: a → ⁧أ⁩ , i → ⁧ئ⁩ , u → ⁧ؤ⁩
The vowel is the loudest between the hamza and the one preceding it: i > u > a > sukūn; i → ⁧ئ⁩ , u → ⁧ؤ⁩ , a → ⁧أ⁩
⁧رَئِيس⁩ raʾīs · ⁧سُؤَال⁩ suʾāl · ⁧مُؤْتَمَر⁩ muʾtamar · ⁧مَسْأَلَة⁩ masʾala · ⁧سَأَلَ⁩ saʾala · ⁧مَسْؤُول⁩ masʾūl

blocks.text: Exceptions to recognize. After a ā long, inside the word, the hamza often stands on the line: ⁧قِرَاءَة⁩ qirāʾa Reading is done. Egypt is often written ⁧مسئول⁩ in place of ⁧مسؤول⁩ : is the same word with a different convention.

blocks.text: 2. Madda, alif maqṣūra and alif short
2.1 The Madda ⁧آ⁩
When a hamza is followed by a ā long, instead of writing ⁧أا⁩ write an alife with a wavy line on it: ⁧آ⁩ = ʾā. Examples: ⁧آخِر⁩ āḫir "Last' is the case, ⁧القُرْآن⁩ al-Qurʾān The Qur'an.
2.2 The alif maqṣūra ⁧ى⁩

The ā long is often written with ⁧ى⁩ , a ⁧ي⁩ no points: ⁧عَلَى⁩ ʿalā "Su" on the ground, ⁧إِلَى⁩ ilā "Verso" is replaced by the following: ⁧مُسْتَشْفَى⁩ mustašfā Hospital: ⁧مُوسَى⁩ Mūsā "Mosè" is the name of the family. It's pronounced exactly like a ā. Attention to the Egyptian press. In Egypt the ⁧ي⁩ The final print is often without points: ⁧علي⁩ may be ʿalā The name of the vessel ʿAlī. The context decides.
2.3 The alif short above the consonant

Some very frequent words have a ā long indicated by a small vertical alif above the consonant ( ⁧ٰـ⁩ ), rather than by a ⁧ا⁩ : ⁧هٰذَا⁩ hāḏā This is the case. ⁧هٰذِهِ⁩ hāḏihi This is the case. ⁧ذٰلِكَ⁩ ḏālika "Those" are: ⁧لٰكِنْ⁩ lākin "Ma', ⁧الله⁩ Allāh, ⁧الرَّحْمٰن⁩ ar-Raḥmān. In texts without vowels the short alif does not appear: ⁧هذا⁩ read anyway hāḏā. These words must be memorized.
3. The tanwīn
The indefinite desinences of the name are written doubling the final vowel sign; they are pronounced with a final n.
⁧ٍـ⁩ tanwīn kasr -in genitive ⁧كِتَابٍ⁩ kitābin
• Undetermined. The tanwīn indicates that the name is indeterminate: ⁧كِتَابٌ⁩ It's a book. Never used together in Article: ⁧الكِتَابُ⁩ al-kitābu.
• The alife of the tanwīn -an. The tanwīn fatḥ is written with a ⁧ا⁩ extra ( ⁧كِتَابًا⁩ ), except after ⁧ة⁩ ( ⁧مَدِينَةً⁩ madīnatan) e after a hamza preceded by ā ( ⁧مَاءً⁩ māʾan).

• Pause. - one and -fall (kitāb); -an becomes -ā in the classical break, but in the daily adverbs you says -an: ⁧شُكْرًا⁩ šukran Thank you. ⁧جِدًّا⁩ ǧiddan Very much. ⁧أَيْضًا⁩ ayḍan "Even" is not included; ⁧عَفْوًا⁩ ʿafwan Please.
• Cases (because -un, -an, -in) are studied in A1-19: now you just have to read them.
4. The alif waṣla

Some words begin with an alif without hamza, the alif waṣla ('linking alife'): it shall be pronounced only at the beginning of a sentence; After a vowel, his vowel falls and the word ties to the previous one. In the Koran is written ⁧اٱ⁩ , in the common texts is a simple ⁧ا⁩ .

rows: At the beginning of the sentence
⁧وَاسْمِي⁩ wa-smī · ⁧بِسْمِ اللهِ⁩ bi-smo llāhi In the name of God

blocks.text: ⁧اِبْن⁩ • child • ⁧اِبْنِي⁩ ibnī My son ⁧وَابْنُهُ⁩ wa-bnuhu ... and his son.

Note: in ⁧فِي البَيْتِ⁩ the ī long fī is pronounced short before the group of consonants: fi l-bayti. Onomastics. In compound names, when ⁧اِبْن⁩ The son of the child is between two own names, he also loses the written alf: ⁧مُحَمَّد بْن سَلْمَان⁩ Muḥammad bin Salmān, literally “Muhammad son of Salman”. The form of the transliterated name ('bin' or 'ben') comes from here (NO-01).

6.1 The words in context
⁧شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا⁩ šukran ǧazīlan Thank you very much.
A security officer has stated............is one of the most frequent attribution formulas in the Arab press: you will meet her again in B2-08.

8. Listening and oral production
Script A · glottis shot
. ⁧مَاء، شَيْء⁩ . ⁧أَمْن، أُمّ، إِرْهَاب⁩ . ⁧أَ، إِ، أُ⁩
Script B · minimum pairs
. ⁧عَلَى، عَلِيّ⁩ . ⁧سَأَلَ، سَعَلَ⁩ . ⁧أَمَل، عَمَل⁩
Script C · dictation
. ⁧لَاجِئ⁩ . ⁧شُكْرًا⁩ . ⁧عَلَى⁩ . ⁧مَاء⁩ . ⁧شَيْء⁩ . ⁧مَسْؤُول⁩ . ⁧أَخْبَار⁩ . ⁧سُؤَال⁩ . ⁧رَئِيس⁩ . ⁧أَمْن⁩
Oral production
1. Glottis in the middle of the word. Read ra-ʾīs, su-ʾāl, mas-ʾūl with a clear interruption.
2. Glottis and ʿayn. ʾamal / ʿamal, saʾala / saʿala: The first is an interruption, the second is an extensionable sound.
3. Tanwīn and pause. Read kitābun, kitāban, kitābinThen kitāb paused; read šukran and ǧiddan.
4. Registration. Timed reading; then read the formulas of the section 6.1.
